review_cost.rationale: I'd approve after a single pass of nits: .gitignore for the build output, cancel the debounce timer, consolidate the three ids→cards blocks, and bound the move fan-out. Nothing requires reworking structure.

findings.issue: The search debounce timer is never cancelled when the home component unmounts; a timer that was armed before the user clicks a card can fire 250 ms later and call nav('/?q=…'), bouncing the user off the page they just navigated to (or throwing against a disposed loader).
findings.suggestion: Cancel the timer on unmount (useCleanup / useTask$ cleanup, or clear it when the route's navigation starts), and ignore the callback once the component is gone.

findings.issue: Production build output (minified SSR and client bundles, 404.html, sitemap.xml) is present under app/ while the repo's .gitignore covers only /data/, /.data-cache/ and node_modules/ — these artifacts would be committed and reviewed as noise.
findings.suggestion: Add app/dist/, app/server/ and app/tmp/ to .gitignore and do not ship them in the source tree.

findings.issue: Unbounded Promise.all fan-out: a Pokémon with a wide movepool triggers up to ~190 concurrent API fetches on a cache miss; the index builders in api.ts (lines 94, 139, 164) do the same for 18-25 records.
findings.suggestion: Bound concurrency (e.g. a small worker-pool map) or avoid fetching whole records when only one field is needed — version groups are fetched entirely for their `order`.

findings.issue: The 'collect ids → exclude alternate forms → dedupe → sort → map to CardData via speciesById' block is duplicated nearly verbatim in abilities/[name]/index.tsx:20-34 and types/[name]/index.tsx:47-61.
findings.suggestion: Extract one helper (e.g. toCardsFor(ids, { note? }) in lib/api.ts or a component helper) and reuse it in all three routes.

findings.issue: API base URL is read from process.env at module load; this only works because routeLoader$ code runs server-side (verified absent from the client bundle), and it silently couples the whole data layer to Node.
findings.suggestion: Read it via requestEvent.env.get('API_BASE_URL') (or pass it through the loader) per the framework's env-variable guidance, keeping the data layer portable.

findings.issue: EXCLUDED_TYPES is defined identically in the route and in lib/api.ts:86 — the exclusion rule lives in two places and can drift.
findings.suggestion: Derive it from the type index (typeIndex.byName.has) or export the constant from lib/api.ts.

findings.issue: A recursive EvoTree component is exported from a route index.tsx; route modules are conventionally reserved for the default component, head and loaders.
findings.suggestion: Move EvoTree to src/components/ alongside the other shared components.

findings.issue: getSpeciesNameById rebuilds a 1025-entry Map on every call (used on every ability, move and type page request).
API response parsing is typed as `any` throughout (api.ts:94-96,139-141,164-166 and every route loader) despite strict:true in tsconfig, so the schema knowledge exists only in the author's head.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the handful of PokeAPI response shapes actually consumed.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache never evicts successful responses, so memory grows monotonically (up to the full dataset) for the process lifetime.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for a fixed snapshot API, but consider a TTL or size cap so the comment's 'live service' claim is honoured over long uptimes.

summary: A clean, current-stable Qwik City app: server-only routeLoader$ data loading, stock adapter and entry scaffolding, minimal dependencies, and spec-accurate 404, pagination and sorting logic. The structure holds up — two well-bounded lib modules and small per-route loaders — with the main drags being three duplicated ids→cards blocks, an uncancelled debounce timer, unbounded per-request fetch fan-out, and build artifacts left unignored. I'd approve after one round of nits.
